nodes.pageTitle: Town of Andover, CT — Resources & Reports
nodes.description: A personally maintained guide to reports, plain-language charter explainers, and other resources about the Town of Andover, Connecticut.
nodes.lede: A personally maintained gateway to research, plain-language explainers, and civic reference material — everything in one place, nothing buried.

sections.label: The Facts
sections.title: Setting the record straight
sections.blurb: Issue-by-issue responses to specific mailers, flyers, or public claims about Andover town business — each edition weighs one piece of public communication against the underlying records.

sections.label: Reports
sections.title: Original analysis
sections.blurb: Longer, sourced pieces compiled to inform specific budget or policy conversations. Each draws directly on official town, regional, or state documents, and each is footnoted to the source.

sections.label: The Town Charter
sections.title: The governing document & plain-language guides
sections.blurb: The Charter itself, restructured for online reading, alongside topic-by-topic explainers that translate it into ordinary English with cross-references to Connecticut state law.

items.title: Town Charter (2024 revision)
items.desc: The current Charter as an interactive, cross-linked TiddlyWiki — a personal rebuild of the official PDF, restructured for online reading, and the source the guides refer back to.

sections.aside: For historical reference, the prior 2022 Charter is archived too — preserved for comparison only; not current.

items.title: The Annual Budget Process
items.gloss: October planning through the May referendum; the contested question of BOF authority over the school budget.

items.title: Town Meetings
items.gloss: The three types, what triggers each, quorum, and the subjects that require a Special Town Meeting.

items.title: Governance Structure
items.gloss: The council-manager model: authority split among Selectmen, First Selectman, and Town Administrator.

items.title: Spending Beyond the Annual Budget
items.gloss: Supplemental and emergency appropriations, the capital reserve, and the rules around bonds.

items.title: Appointments, Vacancies, and Removals
items.gloss: How officials are selected and removed, and the attendance rules that trigger automatic resignation.

items.title: Elections
items.gloss: Which offices are elected, when, and for how long, plus the minority-representation frameworks.

sections.label: Series
sections.title: Longer accounts, in parts
sections.blurb: Extended pieces published as a sequence and then gathered into one continuous account. Each is drawn entirely from the public record, and every claim is sourced.

items.title: A Town Asset
items.desc: An account of the First Selectman's conduct toward the elementary school, drawn entirely from Andover's own minutes, packets, and meeting recordings. Read it as one continuous article, or browse the record below.

items.title: Every part, with its sources
items.desc: All thirteen parts, each with the card that introduced it and a link to its underlying sources.

items.title: The first move onto the grounds
A permit for its own lot, on its own money
The town joins a contract it was not part of
The seat he did not take, until he did
The contract, and the law firm
A question answered, and asked again
Paying to defeat the budget he was there to help create

sections.label: Other
sections.title: Reference material
sections.blurb: Longstanding reference works and archives that don't fit the report or charter-guide format but are part of the same project.

items.title: Meeting Video Archive
items.desc: Recordings of Selectmen, Board of Finance, Board of Education and other public meetings — indexed by date and body, most with searchable, timestamped transcripts.

items.title: Tools
items.desc: Small utilities and machine-readable data files. First up: the town budget, hand-rebuilt from its published PDF into a working spreadsheet you can sort and total.

items.title: The Andover Flyer — Annotated
items.desc: A structured response to the anonymous May 2025 budget flyer — reproduced page-by-page, with the claims walked through against the records that contradict them.

nodes.description: Longstanding reference works and archives about the Town of Andover, Connecticut — tools and data, a public-meeting video archive, and an annotated flyer rebuttal.
Small utilities and machine-readable data about the Town of Andover, Connecticut — starting with a working spreadsheet rebuilt from the town's budget PDF.
